title: Sections of a pulled-back sheaf over a descended affine etale object on a limit of qcqs schemes are the colimit of the sections at the stages (Stacks 09YQ in degree 0)
statement:
Let $I$ be a directed set and $(X_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ whose transition morphisms $f_{ii'}:X_i\to X_{i'}$ ($i\ge i'$) are affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], every $X_i$ being quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with limit $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$ and projections $f_i:X\to X_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $0\in I$, $\mathcal G$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $(X_0)_{\Et}$ (an object of $\Mod((X_0)_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]) and $V_0\to X_0$ an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] with $V_0$ affine, an object of $(X_0)_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For $i\ge0$ put $V_i=V_0\times_{X_0}X_i$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] along $f_{i0}$; an object of $(X_i)_{\Et}$), $V=V_0\times_{X_0}X$ (along $f_0$; an object of $X_{\Et}$), $\mathcal G_i=f_{i0}^{-1}\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal G_\infty=f_0^{-1}\mathcal G$, the inverse images of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] ($f_{00}=\mathrm{id}$, $\mathcal G_0=\mathrm{id}^{-1}\mathcal G$). For $i'\ge i\ge0$ let $\rho_{i'i}:\mathcal G_i(V_i)\to\mathcal G_{i'}(V_{i'})$ be the composite of the unit $\eta:\mathcal G_i\to f_{i'i,*}f_{i'i}^{-1}\mathcal G_i$ on sections over $V_i$, which lands in $(f_{i'i}^{-1}\mathcal G_i)(V_i\times_{X_i}X_{i'})$ by the definition of the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], of the composition isomorphism $c:f_{i'i}^{-1}f_{i0}^{-1}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{i'0}^{-1}\mathcal G$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], and of the restriction along the canonical isomorphism $V_{i'}\xrightarrow{\sim}V_i\times_{X_i}X_{i'}$ of iterated fibre products over $X_{i'}$; let $\rho_i:\mathcal G_i(V_i)\to\mathcal G_\infty(V)$ be defined in the same way from the unit of $f_i^{-1}\dashv f_{i,*}$, the composition isomorphism $f_i^{-1}f_{i0}^{-1}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}f_0^{-1}\mathcal G$ and the canonical isomorphism $V\xrightarrow{\sim}V_i\times_{X_i}X$ over $X$. Then $\rho_{i''i'}\circ\rho_{i'i}=\rho_{i''i}$, $\rho_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho_{i'}\circ\rho_{i'i}=\rho_i$ for $i''\ge i'\ge i\ge0$, and the induced map of $\Lambda$-modules
$$\varinjlim_{i\ge0}\mathcal G_i(V_i)\longrightarrow\mathcal G_\infty(V)$$
is bijective; in particular every $t\in\mathcal G_\infty(V)$ is $\rho_i(s)$ for some $i\ge0$ and some $s\in\mathcal G_i(V_i)$. (Stacks, Etale Cohomology, Theorem 09YQ (theorem-colimit) in degree $p=0$, applied to the system $(V_i)_{i\ge0}$ with limit $V$ and the system of sheaves $\mathcal G_i|_{V_i}$; this is the special case used in the paragraph 'Fully faithful' of the proof of Lemma 09YU.)

proof.text: *The system of etale objects and its limit.* Let $s:V_0\to X_0$ be the given etale morphism and, for $i\ge0$, $p_i:V_i=V_0\times_{X_0}X_i\to X_i$ and $t_{i0}:V_i\to V_0$ the projections, $p:V=V_0\times_{X_0}X\to X$ and $t_0:V\to V_0$ likewise. Base changes of etale morphisms are etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1), so $p_i$, $p$ are etale. The transition morphisms $f_{i0}$ and the projection $f_0$ are affine ([lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]), so their base changes $t_{i0}$, $t_0$ are affine and, $V_0$ being affine, $V_i$ and $V$ are affine [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (1),(2); affine schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit] (with $T=V_0$, $S_i=X_i$), $(V_i,t_{i'i}=\mathrm{id}_{V_0}\times f_{i'i})_{i\in I_{\ge0}}$ is an inverse system over the directed set $I_{\ge0}$ with affine transition morphisms and limit $V$, with projections $t_i=\mathrm{id}_{V_0}\times f_i:V\to V_i$. From the definition of the fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]: $p_i\circ t_{i'i}=f_{i'i}\circ p_{i'}$ and $p_i\circ t_i=f_i\circ p$, and the morphisms $\iota_{i'i}=(t_{i'i},p_{i'}):V_{i'}\to V_i\times_{X_i}X_{i'}$ and $\iota_i=(t_i,p):V\to V_i\times_{X_i}X$ are the canonical isomorphisms of iterated fibre products used in the statement, so these squares are cartesian. Put $w_i=f_{i0}\circ p_i=s\circ t_{i0}:V_i\to X_0$ and $w=f_0\circ p=s\circ t_0:V\to X_0$; then $w_i\circ t_{i'i}=w_{i'}$ and $w_i\circ t_i=w$ (equalities of morphisms, as $t_{i0}\circ t_{i'i}=t_{i'0}$, $t_{i0}\circ t_i=t_0$), and $f_{i0}\circ f_{i'i}=f_{i'0}$, $f_{i0}\circ f_i=f_0$.

proof.text: *Reduction to abelian sheaves; $\Lambda$-linearity.* By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2),(3), for a morphism $u$ the module inverse image $u^{-1}$ has as underlying abelian sheaf the abelian inverse image of the underlying abelian sheaf, and the unit of the module adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ is the unit of the abelian one; in particular the units occurring in $\rho_{i'i}$, $\rho_i$ are $\Lambda$-linear. The composition isomorphism $c_{u,v,G}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] is $\Lambda$-linear: on $\Mod(-,\Lambda)$ both $v^{-1}u^{-1}$ (with the composite unit) and $(u\circ v)^{-1}$ are left adjoint to $u_*v_*\cong(u\circ v)_*$ (through $d_{u,v}$, which is made of restriction maps, hence $\Lambda$-linear), so [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] gives an isomorphism $c'$ of module-valued functors satisfying the unit equation of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2); since the module units are the abelian ones, the underlying abelian map of $c'_G$ satisfies that equation too, so it equals $c_{u,v,G}$ by the uniqueness there. Restriction maps of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules are $\Lambda$-linear. Hence $\rho_{i'i}$ and $\rho_i$ are $\Lambda$-linear, and every assertion of the statement concerns only the underlying maps of abelian groups; from now on $\mathcal G$ is regarded as an abelian sheaf, $\mathcal G_i$, $\mathcal G_\infty$ as its abelian inverse images, and $c$, $\eta$ as those of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

proof.text: *The system of sheaves on the $V_i$ and its colimit.* Put $\mathcal F_i=w_i^{-1}\mathcal G$ on $(V_i)_{\Et}$ and, for $i'\ge i\ge0$, $\varphi_{i'i}=c_{w_i,t_{i'i},\mathcal G}:t_{i'i}^{-1}\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}(w_i\circ t_{i'i})^{-1}\mathcal G=\mathcal F_{i'}$ ([lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2)). The associativity of $c$ ([lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] (1), with $(u,v,w)=(w_i,t_{i'i},t_{i''i'})$) is the cocycle condition $\varphi_{i''i}\circ c_{t_{i'i},t_{i''i'},\mathcal F_i}=\varphi_{i''i'}\circ t_{i''i'}^{-1}\varphi_{i'i}$, and its unit law gives $\varphi_{ii}=c_{w_i,\mathrm{id}}=e_{V_i,\mathcal F_i}$, the identification $\mathrm{id}^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$; so $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i})$ is a system of abelian sheaves on $(V_i,t_{i'i})$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-limit-of-schemes]. Its transition maps on $V$ are $\psi_{i'i}=t_{i'}^{-1}\varphi_{i'i}\circ c_{t_{i'i},t_{i'},\mathcal F_i}^{-1}:t_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i\to t_{i'}^{-1}\mathcal F_{i'}$ (step 1 of that node). Let $\gamma_i=c_{w_i,t_i,\mathcal G}:t_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}w^{-1}\mathcal G$. Associativity of $c$ with $(u,v,w)=(w_i,t_{i'i},t_{i'})$ gives $\gamma_{i'}\circ t_{i'}^{-1}\varphi_{i'i}=\gamma_i\circ c_{t_{i'i},t_{i'},\mathcal F_i}$, i.e. $\gamma_{i'}\circ\psi_{i'i}=\gamma_i$. So the isomorphisms $\gamma_i$ identify the system $(t_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i,\psi)$ with the constant system of value $w^{-1}\mathcal G$ and identity transition maps; as $I_{\ge0}$ is directed, hence connected, the constant cocone is a colimit [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram], and therefore $(w^{-1}\mathcal G,(\gamma_i)_i)$ is a colimit of $(t_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i,\psi)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. We take $\mathcal F=w^{-1}\mathcal G$ with coprojections $\gamma_i$.

proof.text: *Theorem 09YQ in degree $0$.* By step 1 the $V_i$ ($i\ge0$) are quasi-compact and quasi-separated with affine transition morphisms and limit $V$, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-limit-of-schemes] with $p=0$, applied to the system of step 3 and the colimit $(w^{-1}\mathcal G,\gamma_i)$, shows that the maps $\theta_i=H^0(\gamma_i)\circ t_i^*$ induce a bijection $\varinjlim_{i\ge0}H^0((V_i)_{\Et},\mathcal F_i)\to H^0(V_{\Et},w^{-1}\mathcal G)$, the colimit being over the transition maps $H^0(\varphi_{i'i})\circ t_{i'i}^*$, which form a directed system by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (3),(4) and the cocycle condition of step 3. Translate to sections with [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-degree-zero]: the isomorphisms $\epsilon:\Gamma(T,-)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(T_{\Et},-)$ of (1) are natural in the sheaf, and by (2) $t^*\circ\epsilon=\epsilon\circ\eta_t(\text{global sections})$ ([def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]). Hence, with $\sigma_{i'i}=\varphi_{i'i}(V_{i'})\circ\eta_{t_{i'i},\mathcal F_i}(V_i):\mathcal F_i(V_i)\to\mathcal F_{i'}(V_{i'})$ and $\sigma_i=\gamma_i(V)\circ\eta_{t_i,\mathcal F_i}(V_i):\mathcal F_i(V_i)\to(w^{-1}\mathcal G)(V)$ (units on global sections, $(t_*H)(V_i)=H(V_{i'})$, resp. $H(V)$, as in [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]): $\sigma_{i''i'}\circ\sigma_{i'i}=\sigma_{i''i}$, $\sigma_{i'}\circ\sigma_{i'i}=\sigma_i$, and the induced map $\varinjlim_{i\ge0}\mathcal F_i(V_i)\to(w^{-1}\mathcal G)(V)$ is bijective.

proof.text: *Comparison of the two systems.* Let $\rho^{\mathrm{res}}$ denote the isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1) for the etale $p_i$, $p$ (natural in the sheaf), and define the bijections $\alpha_i=c_{f_{i0},p_i,\mathcal G}(V_i)\circ\rho^{\mathrm{res}}_{\mathcal G_i}(V_i)^{-1}:\mathcal G_i(V_i)\to\Gamma(V_i,p_i^{-1}\mathcal G_i)\to\mathcal F_i(V_i)$ and $\alpha=c_{f_0,p,\mathcal G}(V)\circ\rho^{\mathrm{res}}_{\mathcal G_\infty}(V)^{-1}:\mathcal G_\infty(V)\to(w^{-1}\mathcal G)(V)$ ([lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], $w_i=f_{i0}p_i$, $w=f_0p$). Claim: $\alpha_{i'}\circ\rho_{i'i}=\sigma_{i'i}\circ\alpha_i$ and $\alpha\circ\rho_i=\sigma_i\circ\alpha_i$. For the first, let $b\in\mathcal G_i(V_i)$, $a=\rho^{\mathrm{res}}_{\mathcal G_i}(V_i)^{-1}(b)$, $t=t_{i'i}$. [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-pullback-unit] for the cartesian square $(g,p,g',p')=(f_{i'i},p_i,t,p_{i'})$ of step 1 and $F=\mathcal G_i$ gives $(f_{i'i}^{-1}\mathcal G_i)(\iota_{i'i})(\eta_{f_{i'i},\mathcal G_i}(V_i)(b))=\rho^{\mathrm{res}}(V_{i'})(\kappa(V_{i'})(\eta_{t}(V_i)(a)))$ with $\kappa=c_{f_{i'i},p_{i'}}^{-1}\circ c_{p_i,t}$ at $\mathcal G_i$. Apply $c_{f_{i0},f_{i'i},\mathcal G}(V_{i'})$: it commutes with the restriction along $\iota_{i'i}$ (a morphism of sheaves), so the left side becomes $\rho_{i'i}(b)$ by the definition of $\rho_{i'i}$; on the right, naturality of $\rho^{\mathrm{res}}$ moves it inside as $p_{i'}^{-1}(c_{f_{i0},f_{i'i}})$. Hence $\alpha_{i'}(\rho_{i'i}(b))=\bigl[c_{f_{i'0},p_{i'}}\circ p_{i'}^{-1}c_{f_{i0},f_{i'i}}\circ c_{f_{i'i},p_{i'}}^{-1}f_{i0}^{-1}\circ c_{p_i,t}f_{i0}^{-1}\bigr](V_{i'})(\eta_t(V_i)(a))$, which by associativity of $c$ ([lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] (1), $(u,v,w)=(f_{i0},f_{i'i},p_{i'})$) equals $[c_{f_{i0},f_{i'i}p_{i'}}\circ c_{p_i,t}f_{i0}^{-1}](V_{i'})(\eta_t(V_i)(a))$. On the other side, naturality of the unit $\eta_t$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] along the morphism $c_{f_{i0},p_i,\mathcal G}$ gives $\sigma_{i'i}(\alpha_i(b))=[c_{w_i,t}\circ t^{-1}c_{f_{i0},p_i}](V_{i'})(\eta_t(V_i)(a))$, and associativity with $(u,v,w)=(f_{i0},p_i,t)$ turns this into $[c_{f_{i0},p_it}\circ c_{p_i,t}f_{i0}^{-1}](V_{i'})(\eta_t(V_i)(a))$. Since $p_i\circ t=f_{i'i}\circ p_{i'}$ (step 1) the two agree. The second identity is the same computation for the cartesian square $(f_i,p_i,t_i,p)$, with $\iota_i$, $f_{i0}\circ f_i=f_0$ and $p_i\circ t_i=f_i\circ p$.

proof.text: *The system identities.* By step 5, $\rho_{i'i}=\alpha_{i'}^{-1}\sigma_{i'i}\alpha_i$ and $\rho_i=\alpha^{-1}\sigma_i\alpha_i$ (the $\alpha$'s are bijections). Hence $\rho_{i''i'}\rho_{i'i}=\alpha_{i''}^{-1}\sigma_{i''i'}\sigma_{i'i}\alpha_i=\alpha_{i''}^{-1}\sigma_{i''i}\alpha_i=\rho_{i''i}$ and $\rho_{i'}\rho_{i'i}=\alpha^{-1}\sigma_{i'}\sigma_{i'i}\alpha_i=\rho_i$ by step 4. For $\rho_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$: $\sigma_{ii}=\varphi_{ii}(V_i)\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id},\mathcal F_i}(V_i)=e_{V_i,\mathcal F_i}(V_i)\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id},\mathcal F_i}(V_i)$ (step 3), read through $V_i\cong V_i\times_{V_i}V_i$, is the identity by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (3) ($e\circ d\circ\eta=\mathrm{id}$, $d(V_i)$ being restriction along that isomorphism), so $\rho_{ii}=\alpha_i^{-1}\alpha_i=\mathrm{id}$.

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By step 6 the $\Lambda$-modules $\mathcal G_i(V_i)$ with the $\Lambda$-linear maps $\rho_{i'i}$ (step 2) form a directed system with a compatible family $\rho_i$, which induces a $\Lambda$-linear map $\rho:\varinjlim_{i\ge0}\mathcal G_i(V_i)\to\mathcal G_\infty(V)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] (for the ring $\Lambda$, and for $\mathbf Z$ in step 4) the bijectivity of the map induced by a compatible family $(\tau_i)$ out of a directed system $(M_i,\mu_{i'i})$ is equivalent to: (a) every element of the target is $\tau_i(x)$ for some $i$, $x\in M_i$, and (b) $\tau_i(x)=\tau_i(y)$ implies $\mu_{i'i}(x)=\mu_{i'i}(y)$ for some $i'\ge i$ (use (1) and (2) of that lemma with a common upper bound); conditions (a), (b) only involve the underlying sets. Step 4 gives (a), (b) for $(\mathcal F_i(V_i),\sigma_{i'i},\sigma_i)$, and the bijections $\alpha_i$, $\alpha$ carry them to $(\mathcal G_i(V_i),\rho_{i'i},\rho_i)$ by step 5. So $\rho$ is bijective, and (a) is the 'in particular'.

reviewed.note: Reviewed by the lead (opus-relaunch6). Seven steps, one new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-pullback-unit (the unit-side counterpart of 03CF/03EF for a cartesian square with an etale side, agent-identified, with the intended proof recorded in its source). Stacks only says 'a special case of 09YQ'; the split makes it one: the V_i form a directed system of affine schemes with limit V (01YZ), the module statement reduces to the underlying abelian sheaves (prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact (2),(3) and uniqueness of left adjoints for the Lambda-linearity of the composition isomorphism), the system F_i = w_i^{-1}G with the composition isomorphisms as transition maps has colimit w^{-1}G on V (associativity of c from lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition (1), constant diagram), lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-limit-of-schemes in degree 0 translated to sections, the two systems compared through the restriction isomorphisms of lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction and the new node, the system identities and bijectivity via lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise. The nodes of unit sk-def-exchange used are on the route (no route line). Noted: lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-limit-of-schemes step 1 attributes the associativity of c to lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition, which states it only in its derived version (stage-3 note).
